slots.title: Core inflation 0.3% MoM beats 0.2% est.
slots.body:
August core inflation (prices excluding food and energy) rose 0.3% month over month.

The consensus had been 0.2%; July’s core gain was 0.2%.

Headline inflation was 0.4% month over month, matching the estimate.

Year-over-year headline inflation was 3.4%, unchanged from July and on the estimate.

Core inflation over the past year was 2.4%, down from 2.5% in July and in line with the estimate.

Coverage tied the core print to next week’s Federal Reserve meeting on interest rates.

Which part of the CPI report do you watch first — headline or core?

slots.title: U.S. session recap — Sept. 11, 2026
slots.body:
The Sept. 11 U.S. cash session closed with the S&P 500 up 0.8% at 7,655.50, the Nasdaq Composite up 1.0% at 26,333.04, and the Dow up 1.0% at 52,573.29; the Russell 2000 added 0.4% to 2,903.94.

At 12:30 ET the August inflation bundle printed: headline inflation YoY 3.4% (in line with 3.4% expected), month-over-month inflation 0.4% (0.4% expected), and core inflation MoM 0.3% versus 0.2% expected; core YoY was 2.4% versus 2.4% expected.

Later, Michigan consumer sentiment for September came in at 47.8 versus 51.0 expected and 51.7 prior—a high-impact release on the calendar that day.

The CBOE VIX finished at 15.84, down 2.00 points (−11.2%) from 17.84, while same-day market coverage linked equity strength to the inflation read and Fed-meeting context.

On Nasdaq sector averages for the date, real estate led at +1.2%, industrials +0.5%, and basic materials +0.5%; utilities lagged at −1.5%, healthcare −1.0%, and technology −0.5%.

Among megacaps in the feed, $AMZN rose 1.9% to 256.78,:
- $GOOGL 1.8% to 338.50
- $AAPL 1.7% to 332.27
- $AMD 2.5% to 516.13

$UNH fell 2.4% to 379.09.

$KR closed up 2.7% at 58.49 after reporting EPS of 1.09 against a 1.06 estimate and revenue of about $34.62B versus roughly $34.64B estimated.

Oil-linked proxies weakened: Brent crude was down 2.8% at 104.61, and the United States Oil Fund ($USO proxy in the tape) was down 2.2% at 154.90; a same-day headline noted Saudi Arabia shutting a key pipeline amid supply concerns.

Gold futures were nearly unchanged at 4,408.90 (0.0%); the dollar-bullish ETF proxy ($UUP) ticked up 0.1% to 28.07; Bitcoin USD was up 0.1% at 77,283.30.

Overseas indexes in the bundle diverged: Japan’s Nikkei 225 was down 1.9% at 64,011.34, while the FTSE 100 rose 0.4% to 10,650.44 and the Hang Seng slipped 0.6% to 24,805.63.

Treasury snapshot dated 2026-09-09 in the feed showed the 10-year at 4.8% and the 2s10s spread at 0.40 percentage points—context for rates heading into the next Fed meeting week.
